source.title: Lilith: Backdoor Generalization under Training-Inference Trigger Shift
source.authors: Zhou Feng; Jiahao Chen; Chunyi Zhou; Yuan Su; Tianyu Du; Yuwen Pu; Jianhai Chen; Jinbao Li; Shouling Ji

record.tranche_reason: The paper assumes bounded geometric transfer between surrogate and victim models and uses representation alignment to construct trigger families. It does not test whether independently trained models’ representations converge.
record.gate_note: The paper measures activation for trigger variants relative to an anchor in a backdoored model. These results concern alignment among trigger-induced representations, not similarity between independently trained models on the same inputs. Table 3 results are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The paper is a backdoor attack study. It assumes bounded surrogate–victim geometric transfer (Assumption 4, motivated by cited transferability work) and never measures representation similarity between independently trained models. Its 'representation alignment' results (Table 3) concern trigger variants versus an anchor within one backdoored victim, not cross-model convergence. Surrogate-to-victim attack transfer is reported only as attack success, and only for the authors' own method.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that singleton poisoning supports family-wise activation of unseen triggers, with representation alignment to the anchor as the decisive mechanism. They draw no conclusion about convergence across independently trained models.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies backdoor generalization under training–inference trigger shift, not the model-representation convergence methods in the original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Trigger proposal and geometry screening affect family activation: off-subspace variants perform poorly, while feature-filtered random and Sobol variants exceed 90% activation. The paper also reports effects of poisoning rate, victim architecture, dataset, and surrogate-data size on attack performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Within a backdoored ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10, trigger variants kept near the anchor's surrogate representation geometry retain high attack success (91–97%). Random in-subspace variants reach 75% and off-subspace variants about 10%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Backdoor activation by unseen triggers depends on preserving anchor-induced representation geometry within a model. This bears on trigger generalization, not cross-model representational convergence.

fits_no_version.finding: Triggers screened on a surrogate model with disjoint data and architecture achieve high family ASR across five victim architectures (ResNet, VGG, ViT) and five datasets (Table 1). This implies some shared vulnerable geometry, but no representation similarity is measured.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Backdoor triggers optimized on a surrogate's representation geometry transfer to architecturally different victims. This is indirect, behavioural evidence of shared representation structure, not a similarity measurement.

record.problems: The paper assumes bounded surrogate–victim geometric transfer rather than establishing a general property of independently trained models. Its reported alignment results concern trigger variants and attack activation, not similarity of model representations for common inputs.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version results were reported. Other experiments on attack performance, detectors, defenses, and perturbations do not measure model-representation convergence.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep of cross-model representation similarity.
No comparison of features or subspaces across seeds.
No mapping, stitching or relative-representation test. Surrogate-to-victim transfer is assumed (Assumption 4), and only attack success is reported.
No cross-model comparison of features or circuits.
No comparison of similarity metrics or input sets for model-to-model convergence.
No measurement of partial alignment, plateaus or their causes.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T4 / 'assumes' classification is right. Assumption 4 (bounded geometry transfer) is an explicit abstraction, not a test. The Table 1 transfer results are own-method attack performance and are excluded from verdicts.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep measuring representation similarity between independently trained models.
No paired image-caption or vision-language representation alignment measurement.
No comparison of features or subspaces across random seeds.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired interchangeability test between models.
No recurring interpretable features or circuits are compared across models.
No alternative similarity metrics, metric settings, or input distributions are tested for model-to-model convergence.
No test of whether model alignment is incomplete, plateaus, or is explained by shared training data or objectives.
